sections.h2: Selling a house in Upper Merion
sections.html:
Upper Merion covers about 17 square miles of Montgomery County and has an estimated 36,674 residents. A single-family sale here needs no use and occupancy permit. What remains is the standard Pennsylvania sequence: disclosure form, agreement of sale, transfer tax, deed recording and tax proration.

The township sits about 16 miles from Philadelphia and takes in the villages of Gulph Mills, King of Prussia, Swedeland and Swedesburg, plus parts of Radnor and Wayne. A house in Swedesburg and a house near the King of Prussia mall draw different buyers, so the first job is matching your street to the right pool of buyers and the right sale route.

Upper Merion works as an employment center as much as a bedroom suburb, so many buyers want a short commute rather than a large yard. The Schuylkill River forms its northern and eastern edge, Valley Forge National Historical Park fills most of the western end, and the King of Prussia retail and office district sits in the middle.

sections.h2: No use and occupancy permit at sale
sections.html:
For a single-family dwelling, a change of ownership needs no Use and Occupancy Permit, provided the use of the dwelling does not change. Converting a house into a different use is a separate question for the township.

Permits still matter if you did work on the house. Buyers' inspectors and lenders ask about decks, finished basements, sheds, pools and replaced roofs. Pull your own records before you list:

  • Permit review takes up to 15 business days, and inspections need 24 hours' notice, so finishing open work before listing takes weeks, not days.
  • Contractors on residential jobs must be state-registered and put a Pennsylvania HIC number and an insurance certificate on the application.
  • Accessory structures have setbacks by zoning district. In R-1 and R-1A a shed or pool sits 10 feet from the side and rear lines, while R-2 and R-3 require four feet from the side and five feet from the rear.

Call the township's safety and code enforcement office if you cannot tell which zoning district your lot is in. A shed or pool that sits too close to a lot line is the sort of problem a buyer's surveyor finds, so measure before you list and fix or disclose anything that falls short.

Public school students attend the Upper Merion Area School District. Children start at one of five K-4 elementary schools: Bridgeport, Caley Road, Candlebrook, Gulph and Roberts. They move on to Upper Merion Area Middle School for grades 5 through 8 and Upper Merion Area High School for grades 9 through 12. Mother Teresa Regional Catholic School is the parochial option.

Elementary assignment depends on your street, so check with the district before naming a school in the listing.

sections.h2: What do I pay and file when I sell?
sections.html:
The state's share of realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the property's value. Add the local share and the usual total is 2 percent, with the second point going to the municipality and school district. Buyers and sellers commonly divide it. Before you sign, call the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds and confirm the rate for your township and school district.

The seller's disclosure duty comes from 68 Pa.C.S. Section 7303. Fill out the property disclosure statement and hand the buyer a signed, dated copy before the agreement of sale is signed. The form covers the roof, basement, plumbing, wiring, storm water facilities, hazardous substances and flood risk indicators. The Schuylkill runs along two edges of Upper Merion and annual precipitation runs near 48.5 inches, so answer the water questions with care. Act 74 of 2026 amended the land item and added a flood-insurance notice to the chapter.

Behind on property taxes? Twice a year, in September and December, the county Tax Claim Bureau auctions parcels that owe taxes from two years back, and winning bidders inherit any liens. For the annual appeal deadline and forms, contact the Board of Assessment Appeals.

At the closing table the title agent totals your mortgage payoff, the transfer tax, any unpaid taxes and prorated tax for the year. You sign the deed, and the agent sends it to the Recorder of Deeds. Ask for a net sheet ahead of time so no line item surprises you.

If the house has unpermitted work, disclose what you know on the form. Applying for a permit on the open work before listing is common, because inspectors notice a deck or finished basement and lenders may ask about it.

sections.h2: If the house needs work before you sell
sections.html:
Repairs and permits go together. Decks, finished basements, sheds, pools and replaced roofs each have their own permit category, and the township can tell you which one your project falls under. Gather the permit numbers, contractor names and final inspection dates in one folder so a buyer's agent can see them at a glance. Start with the oldest items on your list, since a permit review runs up to 15 business days and then an inspector needs a day's notice.

If you would rather not manage contractors, a buyer who purchases as is will price the work into an offer and handle the permits afterward. That trade usually costs you some of the sale price, but it saves weeks and keeps your attention on the move.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits an Upper Merion house best?
sections.html:
Your time and repair budget point to the right route. A listing can tap the big pool of workers around King of Prussia, at the cost of showings, inspection requests and a financing schedule. A private sale saves an agent's fee and adds legal and marketing work. A direct sale to an as-is buyer shortens the schedule and removes repair negotiations, usually at a lower price.

  • Get proof of funds and a dated closing commitment from each buyer.
  • Request a net sheet that shows transfer tax, payoff, tax proration and any repair credits.
  • Judge each route by the money you keep, not the advertised price.

faqs.q: Is a certificate needed to sell a house in Upper Merion Township?
faqs.a: Not for a single-family home that keeps the same use. Ask the township office first if the property is multi-unit or non-residential.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Upper Merion?
faqs.a: The middle owner-reported value is $455,300. Individual houses price off nearby sales, so ask an agent or appraiser for comparables on your street.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when an Upper Merion house sells?
faqs.a: Nothing in the law assigns it. Agreements commonly divide it, though the buyer answers if the amount paid is challenged. Write the split into your agreement of sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Upper Merion house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but disclose what you know. Pennsylvania's disclosure form asks about additions, remodeling and structural changes, and a seller cannot make statements the seller knows are false. Many owners apply for a permit on the open work before listing.

faqs.q: How quickly can a cash sale close in Upper Merion?
faqs.a: With no lender involved, the pace is set by the title search, the deed and the transfer tax paperwork. Get a written date from the buyer, along with a list of what must happen first.
